#### Figure 2 Map 
#### Completed via in Canva customization adding legend and inset map

```{r}
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(here)
library(maps)  # for inset map

# ----------------------------
# Load data
# ----------------------------
file_path <- here("data", "raw","MetroVan_LCC_2020_Final.tif")
lcc2020 <- rast(file_path)

load(here("data", "sites_3857.Rdata"))
sites_3857 <- sites_3857[-c(8),]  # remove one site if needed

sites_matched <- st_transform(sites_3857, crs(lcc2020))

# Crop raster to sites + buffer
site_extent <- ext(vect(sites_matched))
site_extent_buffered <- ext(
  xmin(site_extent) - 1500,
  xmax(site_extent) + 1500,
  ymin(site_extent) - 1500,
  ymax(site_extent) + 1500
)
lcc2020_crop <- crop(lcc2020, site_extent_buffered)

# Land cover classes
lc_classes <- data.frame(
  value = 1:14,
  label = c(
    "Buildings", "Paved", "Other Built", "Barren", "Soil",
    "Coniferous", "Shrub","Deciduous", "Modified Grass",
    "Natural Grass", "Non-Photo Veg.", "Shadow",
    "Water", "Snow/Ice"
  )
)
levels(lcc2020_crop) <- lc_classes

earthy_colors <- c(
  "firebrick", "#7f7f7f", "pink", "lightyellow", "brown4",
  "#1b7837", "green", "#4daf4a", "darkolivegreen1",
  "darkolivegreen3", "lemonchiffon2", "black", "#2c7bb6", "#ffffff"
)

# Site labels
site_labels <- c(
  "Collingwood", "McKenzie", "Shaugnessy", "Queen Elizabeth",
  "False Creek", "Downtown", "West End", "43 & Churchill",
  "14 & Spruce", "19 & Yukon", "Strathcona", "2nd Beach"
)

# Centroids & label offsets
site_centroids <- st_centroid(sites_matched)
label_coords <- st_coordinates(site_centroids)

# Bottom of map for “center” push
bottom_y <- min(label_coords[,2]) - 500
center_x <- mean(label_coords[,1])
label_center <- c(center_x, bottom_y)

# Direction vectors and normalization
dx <- label_coords[,1] - label_center[1]
dy <- label_coords[,2] - label_center[2]
dist <- sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2)
dx_norm <- dx / dist
dy_norm <- dy / dist
push_dist <- 550

label_coords_offset <- label_coords
label_coords_offset[,1] <- label_coords[,1] + dx_norm * push_dist
label_coords_offset[,2] <- label_coords[,2] + dy_norm * push_dist

# Specific vertical adjustments
i_col <- which(site_labels == "Collingwood")
i_mck <- which(site_labels == "McKenzie")
label_coords_offset[i_col,2] <- label_coords_offset[i_col,2] + 120
label_coords_offset[i_mck,2] <- label_coords_offset[i_mck,2] + 300
label_coords_offset[i_col,1] <- label_coords_offset[i_col,1] - 120
label_coords_offset[i_mck,1] <- label_coords_offset[i_mck,1] + 300

# ----------------------------
# Plot figure
# ----------------------------

pdf(here("figs", "Figure2.pdf"), width = 15, height = 12)

# 1. Layout: main map + legend
layout(matrix(c(1,2), ncol = 2), widths = c(4,1))
par(mar = c(3,4,3,0))

# Main map
plot(lcc2020_crop,
     main = "",
     col = earthy_colors,
     type = "classes",
     axes = FALSE,
     legend = FALSE)
plot(st_geometry(sites_matched), add = TRUE, lwd = 4, border = "black")

# Labels with halo
segments(label_coords[,1], label_coords[,2],
         label_coords_offset[,1], label_coords_offset[,2],
         col = "black", lwd = 3)
offsets <- expand.grid(dx = c(-1,0,1), dy = c(-1,0,1))
for(i in 1:nrow(offsets)) {
  if(offsets$dx[i]!=0 | offsets$dy[i]!=0){
    text(label_coords_offset[,1]+offsets$dx[i]*20,
         label_coords_offset[,2]+offsets$dy[i]*20,
         labels = site_labels,
         cex=1.5,font=2,col="black")
  }
}
text(label_coords_offset,
     labels=site_labels,cex=1.5,font=2,col="white")

# -------------------
# North arrow (triangle style)
# -------------------
x_arrow <- xmax(site_extent_buffered) - 1000
y_arrow <- ymax(site_extent_buffered) - 1000
arrow_height <- 600
arrow_width <- 200
polygon(x=c(x_arrow-arrow_width/2, x_arrow+arrow_width/2, x_arrow),
        y=c(y_arrow, y_arrow, y_arrow+arrow_height),
        col="black")
text(x_arrow, y_arrow + arrow_height + 200, "N", font=2, cex=1.5)

# -------------------
# Scale bar upper-left
# -------------------
scale_x <- xmin(site_extent_buffered) + 500
scale_y <- ymax(site_extent_buffered) - 700
rect(scale_x, scale_y, scale_x + 500, scale_y + 50, col="black")
rect(scale_x + 500, scale_y, scale_x + 1000, scale_y + 50, col="white")
text(scale_x + 250, scale_y + 100, "500 m", cex=1.2)
text(scale_x + 750, scale_y + 100, "1000 m", cex=1.2)

# -------------------
# Inset map (top-right)
# -------------------
par(fig=c(0.65,0.95,0.7,0.95), new=TRUE, mar=c(0,0,0,0))
map("world", regions=c("Canada","USA"), fill=TRUE, col="lightgrey", border="white", lwd=0.5)
study_centroid <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_union(sites_matched)))
points(study_centroid[,1], study_centroid[,2], pch=19, col="red", cex=2)

# -------------------
# Legend (right panel)
# -------------------
par(mar=c(2,0,2,0))
plot.new()
plot.window(xlim=c(0,1), ylim=c(0,1))
legend(x=-0.13, y=0.7,
       legend=lc_classes$label,
       fill=earthy_colors,
       border="black",
       cex=1.8,
       bty="n",
       title="Land Cover",
       xjust=0)

dev.off()
```
### Figures 3 and 4

Revised November 2026. Figures 3 and 4 use the main model set by `main_model` in the chunk
below: **F123** (default), with the three socio-political scales (Housing-tenure—density,
Deprivation, Disenfranchisement) on the quantity of food waste and service roads on its presence,
or **F123_all**, with the three scales on both parts. Both are fit to the corrected 3-factor,
16-variable factor scores. Inputs come from the revised analysis steps listed in `src/run_revised_analysis.R`
(factor analysis, fits, predictions, population-density mask).

Outputs:

- `figs/Figure3.pdf`: (a) posterior effects on quantity and presence, oriented so that
  higher scale values are the less privileged condition; (b) expected food waste score.
- `figs/Figure4.pdf`: (a) process model and (b) proxy model on a shared scale,
  (c) proxy on its own scale, (d) ratio of process to proxy predictions.

Dissemination areas with population density below 650 persons km^-2^ are not shown
(`src/domain_mask.R`).

```{r figures-3-4}
local({
  library(here)
  library(sf)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(ggridges)
  library(scales)
  library(viridisLite)
  library(cowplot)
  library(scico)
  library(rstan)

  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------
  ## Inputs
  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------
  ## ---- Main model ------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## "F123":     the three scales on quantity only; service roads on presence (main model)
  ## "F123_all": the three scales on both quantity and presence
  if (!exists("main_model")) main_model <- "F123"   # set once in the setup chunk
  model_cfg <- list(
    F123     = list(fit = "fit_hier_ZIW_16var_F123.Rdata",
                    pars = c("beta1", "beta2", "beta3", "delta1")),
    F123_all = list(fit = "fit_hier_ZIW_16var_F123_all.Rdata",
                    pars = c("beta1", "beta2", "beta3", "delta1", "delta2", "delta3", "delta4"))
  )
  cfg <- model_cfg[[main_model]]
  cat("Main model:", main_model, "\n")

  env <- new.env()
  load(here("data", cfg$fit), envir = env)
  post <- rstan::extract(get(ls(env)[1], envir = env),
                         pars = cfg$pars)
  rm(env); gc()

  load(here("data", "van_dat_predictions_16var.Rdata"))   # van_dat_fa
  stopifnot(all(c(paste0("pred_", main_model), "pred_proxy") %in% names(van_dat_fa)))
  van_dat_fa$pred_main <- van_dat_fa[[paste0("pred_", main_model)]]

  ## Cells in masked DAs (domain_mask.R: population density below the threshold) are removed
  mask_col <- "grey85"
  if ("in_domain" %in% names(van_dat_fa)) {
    ## Masked DAs are removed from the maps entirely (drawn as empty space)
    cat("Removing", sum(!van_dat_fa$in_domain), "masked cells from the maps\n")
    van_dat_fa <- van_dat_fa[van_dat_fa$in_domain, ]
  } else {
    cat("No in_domain column found: run src/domain_mask.R to mask parkland/unpopulated cells.\n")
  }

  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------
  ## Shared stretched colour scale for expected FW score
  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------
  rng <- range(c(van_dat_fa$pred_main, van_dat_fa$pred_proxy), na.rm = TRUE)
  data_at <- approx(c(0, 0.20, 0.90, 1), c(rng[1], 0.25, 1, rng[2]),
                    xout = seq(0, 1, length.out = 101))$y
  brks <- c(c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)[c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1) > rng[1]], rng[2])
  stretched_fill <- function(name = "Expected FW Score") {
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colours = inferno(101), values = scales::rescale(data_at, from = rng), limits = rng,
      na.value = mask_col,
      breaks = brks,
      labels = c(format(brks[-length(brks)], drop0trailing = TRUE), signif(rng[2], 3)),
      name = name
    )
  }
  cat("Shared colour range:", signif(rng, 3), "\n")

  ## =========================================================
  ## Figure 3
  ## =========================================================

  ## (a) Ridge plot: quantity effects (purple) and presence effects (orange).
  ##
  ## Signs are re-expressed for readability; no refit is needed, because the model is linear in
  ## each factor and every coefficient prior is symmetric around 0, so reversing a scale gives the
  ## same model with the coefficient's sign reversed.
  ##   * Presence: the model's zero-inflation part is P(NO waste); the log-odds of presence are
  ##     minus those of absence, so every delta is multiplied by -1.
  ##   * Housing-tenure-density is reoriented so HIGH = denser, more renter-occupied
  ##     (the factor as fitted has high = affluent, low-density): multiply its effects by -1.
  ##   * Enfranchisement is reoriented as DISenfranchisement, HIGH = less employment:
  ##     multiply its effects by -1.
  ##   * Deprivation keeps its orientation (HIGH = more deprived).
  ## Net multipliers on the fitted parameters:
  ##   beta1 (Housing, quantity)   -1     delta1 (roads, presence)              -1
  ##   beta2 (Deprivation, quant.) +1     delta2 (Deprivation, presence)        -1
  ##   beta3 (Enfranch., quantity) -1     delta3 (Housing, presence)  -1 x -1 = +1
  ##                                      delta4 (Enfranch., presence) -1 x -1 = +1
  ## Reorient Housing and Enfranchisement the same way in any factor maps and loading plots.
  sign_flip <- c(beta1 = -1, beta2 = 1, beta3 = -1,
                 delta1 = -1, delta2 = -1, delta3 = 1, delta4 = 1)
  ## One row per scale; quantity (purple) and presence (orange) overlaid, explained by a legend.
  row_of <- c(beta1 = "Housing-tenure\u2014density", beta2 = "Deprivation", beta3 = "Disenfranchisement",
              delta1 = "Service roads", delta3 = "Housing-tenure\u2014density",
              delta2 = "Deprivation", delta4 = "Disenfranchisement")
  part_of <- c(beta1 = "Effect on quantity", beta2 = "Effect on quantity", beta3 = "Effect on quantity",
               delta1 = "Effect on presence", delta2 = "Effect on presence",
               delta3 = "Effect on presence", delta4 = "Effect on presence")
  row_order <- c("Service roads", "Housing-tenure\u2014density", "Deprivation", "Disenfranchisement")
  part_colors <- c("Effect on quantity" = "purple", "Effect on presence" = "orange")

  pars_a <- intersect(names(sign_flip), cfg$pars)
  posterior_long <- as.data.frame(mapply(function(p, f) p * f, post[pars_a], sign_flip[pars_a],
                                         SIMPLIFY = FALSE)) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "value") |>
    mutate(scale_row = factor(row_of[parameter], levels = rev(row_order)),   # first row on top
           part = factor(part_of[parameter], levels = names(part_colors)))

  cat("\nFigure 3a, re-expressed effects: median [95% interval]\n")
  print(posterior_long |>
          group_by(scale_row, part) |>
          summarise(median = round(median(value), 2),
                    lo = round(quantile(value, 0.025), 2),
                    hi = round(quantile(value, 0.975), 2), .groups = "drop") |>
          arrange(desc(scale_row), part))

  plot_3a <- ggplot(posterior_long,
                    aes(x = value, y = scale_row, fill = part, group = interaction(scale_row, part))) +
    geom_density_ridges(scale = 0.9, alpha = 0.6, color = "white", rel_min_height = 0.01) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = part_colors, name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Coefficient Value", y = NULL) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8),
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.justification = "right",
      legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
      legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"),
      legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
      plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2)
    )

  ## (b) Expected FW score map
  map_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, hjust = 0),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
      legend.position = "right",
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
    )

  plot_3b <- ggplot(van_dat_fa) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = pred_main), color = NA) +
    stretched_fill() +
    map_theme +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2),
          legend.justification = "center",
          legend.box.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, -10)) +
    coord_sf(expand = FALSE)

  ## Layout: share of the figure height given to the map (b); panel (a) gets the rest.
  ## Increase map_share to squish (a) further.
  fig3_height <- 6.0    # inches
  map_share   <- 0.64
  fig3 <- ggdraw() +
    draw_plot(plot_3a, x = 0, y = map_share, width = 1, height = 1 - map_share - 0.02) +
    draw_plot(plot_3b, x = 0, y = 0,         width = 1, height = map_share) +
    draw_plot_label(label = c("(a)", "(b)"), x = c(0.015, 0.015), y = c(0.995, map_share + 0.005),
                    size = 14, fontface = "bold")

  ggsave(here("figs", "Figure3.pdf"), fig3, width = 4.875, height = fig3_height, dpi = 300)

  ## =========================================================
  ## Figure 4
  ## =========================================================
  pred_diff <- log10(van_dat_fa$pred_main) - log10(van_dat_fa$pred_proxy)
  cat("Log10 ratio (process / proxy): ", paste(signif(range(pred_diff), 3), collapse = " to "), "\n")

  plot_4a <- ggplot(van_dat_fa) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = pred_main), color = NA) +
    stretched_fill() + map_theme

  plot_4b <- ggplot(van_dat_fa) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = pred_proxy), color = NA) +
    stretched_fill() + map_theme

  plot_4c <- ggplot(van_dat_fa) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = pred_proxy), color = NA) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "inferno", name = "Expected FW Score",
                         labels = function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x), na.value = mask_col) +
    map_theme

  van_dat_fa$pred_diff <- pred_diff

  ## Even (symmetric) diverging scale with a neutral band around 0. The limits are +/- the larger
  ## of |1st percentile| and |99th percentile|; values beyond take the end colours. Legend in ratios.
  q <- quantile(pred_diff, c(0.01, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE)
  L  <- max(abs(q), 0.01)            # symmetric limits: same range on both sides of 0
  lo <- -L; hi <- L
  cat("Log10 ratio quantiles:\n"); print(signif(quantile(pred_diff, c(0, .01, .05, .25, .5, .75, .95, .99, 1)), 3))
  ## Neutral band: cells where the models are within this factor of each other get the
  ## neutral colour (1.25 means ratios between 0.8x and 1.25x). Widen or narrow as needed.
  neutral_ratio <- 1.25
  band <- log10(neutral_ratio)
  L <- max(L, 2 * band); lo <- -L; hi <- L

  ## vik (Crameri Scientific Colour Maps): perceptually uniform and colour-vision-deficiency
  ## friendly. begin/end drop the darkest 15% at each end so the extremes are less dark.
  n_side <- 50
  vik_cols <- scico(2 * n_side + 1, palette = "vik", begin = 0.15, end = 0.85)
  mid_col  <- vik_cols[n_side + 1]
  cols_d <- c(vik_cols[1:n_side], mid_col, mid_col, vik_cols[(n_side + 2):(2 * n_side + 1)])
  vals_d <- c(seq(lo, -band, length.out = n_side + 1)[-(n_side + 1)],   # blue ramp up to -band
              -band, band,                                              # flat neutral band
              seq(band, hi, length.out = n_side + 1)[-1])               # red ramp from +band
  ## Legend ticks: evenly spaced in log, symmetric around 1x (the neutral band is not labelled)
  ratio_brks <- c(1/10, 1/5, 1/2, 1, 2, 5, 10)
  ratio_brks <- ratio_brks[log10(ratio_brks) >= lo & log10(ratio_brks) <= hi]
  ratio_lab  <- ifelse(ratio_brks < 1, paste0("1/", round(1 / ratio_brks), "\u00d7"),
                       paste0(ratio_brks, "\u00d7"))

  plot_4d <- ggplot(van_dat_fa) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = pred_diff), color = NA) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colours = cols_d, values = scales::rescale(vals_d, from = c(lo, hi)),
                         limits = c(lo, hi), oob = squish, na.value = mask_col,
                         breaks = log10(ratio_brks), labels = ratio_lab,
                         name = "Ratio") +
    guides(fill = guide_colourbar(barheight = unit(10, "lines"))) +
    map_theme

  ## Build each panel on its own first, so any error stops the script with its real message
  ## (cowplot otherwise draws a blank space in place of a panel that fails).
  for (nm in c("plot_4a", "plot_4b", "plot_4c", "plot_4d")) {
    cat("Building", nm, "...\n")
    invisible(ggplotGrob(get(nm)))
  }

  ## Panel titles as grid labels, so they sit at the same position in every panel
  fig4 <- plot_grid(
    plot_4a, plot_4b, plot_4c, plot_4d,
    ncol = 2, align = "hv", axis = "tblr",
    labels = c("(a) Process model", "(b) Proxy model",
               "(c) Proxy model (own scale)", "(d) Process \u00f7 proxy"),
    label_size = 13, hjust = 0, label_x = 0.02, label_y = 0.99
  )
  ggsave(here("figs", "Figure4.pdf"), fig4, device = "pdf",
         width = 10, height = 8.3333334, units = "in")

  cat("\nDone: Figure3.pdf, Figure4.pdf (main model:", main_model, ")\n")
})
```

The previous Figure 3 and 4 code (two-factor model with Factor 1 and Factor 3 from a superseded
factor analysis, and city scores computed by projecting city-standardized data onto the loadings)
has been removed; see the git history of this file.
